p.seg: *Lí Sāo Jīng* (The Lament)
I am a descendant of the Emperor Gāoyáng;
My late father was named Bóyōng.
When Jupiter was in the sign of *Shètí* in the first month,
On the day *gēngyín*, I was born.
My father examined and considered my first measures,
And thereupon bestowed upon me a good name.
He named me Zhèngzé,
And styled me Língjūn.
Already I possessed these inner virtues,
And further embellished them with accomplishments.
I wore *jiānglí* and *bìzhǐ*,
And strung autumn orchids to make a pendant.
I hurried as though I would not catch up,
Fearing that the years would not wait for me.
In the morning, I plucked magnolias on the hillside,
In the evening, I gathered winter foliage on the islets.
The sun and moon swiftly pass and do not linger,
Spring and autumn succeed each other in turn.
Seeing the withering of grass and trees,
I fear the aging of the fair one.
Why not seize the prime of life and discard the impure?
Why not change this course?
I will mount a *qí jì* and gallop forth,
Come, I will lead the way!
In the past, the three sage rulers were truly pure,
Indeed, it is the place where all fragrant plants gather.
Intermingling *Shēnjiāo* and *jùnguì*,
How could it be just stringing together *huì* and *chǎi*?
Those wise and upright Yáo and Shùn,
Already followed the Dao and found the right path.
Why were Jié and Zhòu so reckless?
Because they only took shortcuts, leading to troubled steps.
Those partisans who steal pleasure,
Their path is dark, obscure, treacherous and narrow.
Is it that I fear calamity for myself?
I fear that the imperial carriage will be ruined.
Suddenly rushing about, sometimes ahead, sometimes behind,
I followed in the footsteps of the former kings.
Quán did not understand my true feelings,
But instead believed slander and became angrily resentful.
I knew that bluntness would bring trouble,
But I endured it and could not abandon it.
I point to the nine heavens as my witness,
It is only for the sake of *Língxiū*.
We agreed to meet at dusk,
But in the middle of the way, he changed his route.
In the beginning, he made an agreement with me,
But later regretted it, hid away, and had other plans.
I am not troubled by parting,
But I grieve that *Língxiū* changes his mind so often.
I have planted nine *wǎn* of orchids,
And also planted a hundred *mǔ* of *huì*.
I plant *yí* and *jiēchē* in my garden rows,
Intermingling *dùhéng* and fragrant *zhǐ*.
I hope their branches and leaves will grow tall and lush,
And wait for the time when I shall harvest them.
Though they wither and die, what harm is there?
I grieve for the wild and overgrown state of all fragrant plants.
Everyone rushes forward greedily,
Insatiably pursuing their desires.
They are lenient with themselves while measuring others,
Each stirring up jealousy in their hearts.
Suddenly galloping off in pursuit,
This is not what my heart desires.
Old age is gradually approaching,
I fear my good name will not be established.
In the morning, I drink the dew that has fallen on magnolias,
In the evening, I eat the fallen petals of autumn chrysanthemums.
If my feelings are truly beautiful and refined,
What harm is there in a long life of hardship?
I gather tree roots to bind *chǎi*,
And thread together the fallen pistils of *bìlì*.
I bend cinnamon mushrooms to string together *huì*,
And seek *húshéng* to bind them elaborately.
I earnestly follow the ways of former worthies,
Which are not accepted by the worldly.
Though I may not be agreeable to the people of today,
I wish to adhere to the precepts left by Péng Xián.
I sigh deeply and wipe away my tears,
Grieving for the many hardships of the people's lives.
Although I love elegance and self-cultivation, I am restrained and fettered;
With earnest remonstrations in the morning, I am dismissed by evening.
Having dismissed me for wearing fragrant orchids,
They further accuse me of adorning myself with fragrant *chǎi* plants.
Yet this is what my heart delights in;
Even if I die nine times, I would still not regret it.
I resent Líng Xiū's (靈脩) extravagance;
In the end, he does not understand the people's hearts.
The many women are jealous of my beautiful eyebrows;
With rumors and slander, they accuse me of being promiscuous.
Indeed, it is the artfulness of the times,
To turn away from the compass and square and alter what is right.
Turning their backs on the plumb line and ink rope to pursue crookedness,
They compete to accommodate others as the standard.
Depressed and gloomy, I am disheartened;
I alone am in poverty and distress at this time.
I would rather die suddenly and drift away;
I cannot bear to behave in this manner.
The birds of prey do not flock together;
This has been true since ancient times.
How can the square and the round accommodate each other?
How can those with different paths live in peace together?
To suppress my heart and restrain my will,
To endure blame and ward off disgrace,
To sacrifice my purity and integrity to die for righteousness,
This is what the former sages valued.
I regret not examining the path I was on carefully;
Yán zhù hū wú jiāng fǎn.
Turn my chariot to retrace the road,
before I stray too far.
I lead my horse on the orchid bank,
and gallop to Pepper Hill to rest.
Advancing brings blame,
retreating will restore my original attire.
I make clothes from water caltrop and lotus leaves,
and gather lotus blossoms for a skirt.
If they do not understand me, so be it,
so long as my heart truly believes in fragrance.
I raise my towering hat high,
and lengthen my long and splendid pendants.
Fragrance and filth are mixed together,
but my clear essence remains undiminished.
Suddenly turning back to survey the landscape,
I will go and look upon the four desolate regions.
My pendants are adorned with colorful profusion,
their fragrance grows ever more apparent.
People each have their own pleasures,
but I alone love self-cultivation as a constant.
Even if my body is dismembered, I will not change,
how could my heart be punished?
Nǚ Xū's charming demeanor,
repeatedly scolded me.
She said, "Gǔn was stubborn and forthright and lost his life,
ultimately dying in the wilderness of Yǔ.
Why are you so learned and eloquent, and fond of self-cultivation?
Alone, you possess such excellent virtue.
The *cílùshī* plant fills the room,
But you resolutely stand apart and do not follow.
The multitude cannot be persuaded one by one,
Who will say they understand my inner feelings?
The world flocks together and loves cliques,
Why am I so alone and not listened to?
I rely on the former sages to regulate my inner self,
Sighing, I rely on my heart to endure this.
Crossing the Yuán 沅 and Xiāng 湘 rivers, I journey south,
To approach Chóng Huá 重華 and present my words:
[They] initiated the *Jiǔ Biàn* 《九辯》 and the *Jiǔ Gē* 《九歌》,
The Xià 夏 dynasty indulged in leisure and pleasure.
Not considering difficulties to plan for the future,
The five sons thereby lost their family inheritance.
Yì 羿 indulged in roaming and unrestrained hunting,
And also loved to shoot at the large foxes.
Truly, those who create chaos rarely have a good ending,
Zhuó 浞 then coveted his family.
Jiāo 澆 was clad in armor by the strong state of Yǔ 圉,
Indulging in desires without restraint.
Daily indulging in leisure and forgetting himself,
His head was thus smashed and he perished.
Xià Jié 夏桀 constantly acted contrary to virtue,
And consequently met with disaster.
Hòu Xīn 后辛 was minced into meat paste,
And the Yīn 殷 dynasty thereby did not last long.
Tāng and Yǔ were solemn and reverent,
The Zhōu dynasty discussed the Dao without the slightest error.
They promoted the worthy and entrusted the capable,
Following the plumb line and ink without deviation.
August Heaven has no private favor,
It selects and assists based on the people's virtue.
For only the wise and sagacious can have flourishing conduct,
If only they can be employed upon this lower earth.
Looking forward and reflecting backward,
Observing and considering the ultimate plans of the people.
Who is there who is not righteous yet can be used?
Who is there who is not good yet can be made subservient?
Even if my body faces danger and death,
Reviewing my beginnings, I would still have no regrets.
To not measure the mortise before shaping the tenon,
Would surely cause the former sages to be pickled and minced.
I heave a sigh, so melancholy and oppressed,
Grieving that my time is not appropriate.
I gather fragrant orchids to wipe away my tears,
Soaking my lapels with endless weeping.
I kneel and spread my mat to offer my words,
Brightly I have obtained this central correctness;
Driving a team of jade dragons, riding the yí (a mythical bird),
Swiftly, I ride the whirlwind upwards.
At dawn, I set out from Cāngwú,
By evening, I arrive at Xuánpǔ;
Desiring to linger a little by these divine gates,
The sun hastens, about to set.
I order Xī Hé to slow his pace,
Gaze towards Yānzī and not urge him on.
The road is long and stretches far,
I will go above and below to seek.
I let my horses drink in Xiánchí,
And gather the reins at Fúsāng.
I break off a Ruò tree branch to brush away the sun,
And leisurely wander about.
I send the moon god Wàng Shū ahead as vanguard,
And behind, I order the wind god Fēi Lián to hasten in attendance.
The *luán* and *huáng* birds warn me in advance,
And the thunder master tells me of preparations not yet complete.
I order the phoenix to soar,
Following it day and night.
The swirling winds gather and disperse,
Guiding the clouds and rainbows to serve me.
In bustling clusters, they separate and join,
Mottled and resplendent, ascending and descending.
I order the gatekeeper of the Celestial Emperor to open the gate,
And lean against the Chānghé gate, awaiting me.
The time is dim, soon to end,
I knot fragrant orchids and linger long.
The world is turbid and indistinguishable,
Fond of concealing beauty and harboring jealousy.
In the morning, I will cross the White Waters,
Climb Làngfēng and tether my horses.
Suddenly, I turn back with tears flowing,
Alas, on Gāo Qiū 高丘 there are no maidens.
Suddenly I wander in this spring palace,
Breaking off a jade branch to attach to my girdle.
While the glory and splendor have not yet faded,
Let me ask a lower maiden if she is available to be gifted.
I ordered Fēng Lóng 豐隆 to ride the clouds,
Seeking where Mì Fēi 宓妃 might be.
I untied my girdle tassels to pledge my word,
And ordered Jiǎn Xiū 蹇脩 to manage the affair.
Confused and in crowds they parted and met,
Hastily spinning around, it was hard to move forward.
In the evening, she returned and rested at Qióng Shí 窮石,
In the morning, she washed her hair in the Wěi Pán 洧盤.
Preserving her beauty with arrogance,
Daily in pleasure and licentious wandering.
Although truly beautiful, she was without propriety,
So I departed, rejected her, and sought another.
Examining and observing in all four corners,
Circulating throughout the heavens, then I descended.
Gazing at the rising and towering Yáo Tái 瑤臺,
I saw the unmarried maiden of Yǒu Sōng 有娀.
I ordered the zhěn bird to be my matchmaker,
But the zhěn bird told me she was unfavorable.
The male dove flies away cooing,
I still hated its frivolous and skillful ways.
My heart hesitated and was full of doubt,
I wanted to please myself but could not.
The phoenix had already received a commission,
Fearing that Gāo Xīn 高辛 would precede me.
Desiring to gather far and wide but with nowhere to rest,
I will but drift and wander, carefree.
When Shǎo Kāng 少康 had not yet married,
He stayed with the Two Yáo 姚 of Yǒu Yú 有虞.
His reasoning was weak and his matchmaker inept,
I feared that the marriage proposal would not be secure.
The world is muddled and jealous of the worthy,
Favoring the concealing of beauty and the praising of ugliness.
The inner chambers are already so deep and remote,
Yet the wise king is still not awakened.
Keeping my feelings inside without expressing them,
How can I bear to endure this forever?
Searching for qióng máo 藑茅 and tíng chún 筳蓴,
I commanded Líng Fēn 靈氛 to divine for me.
He said, "Two beautiful ones will surely unite;
Who believes in cultivating oneself and yearning for them?
Considering the vastness of the nine provinces,
How could she be the only woman there is?
Strive to go far away and have no doubts;
Who seeks beauty and would release you?
What place is uniquely without fragrant grasses?
Why do you cherish your old home?"
The world is dark and bedazzled,
Who can truly discern my good and evil?
The people's likes and dislikes are different,
Only this group of people are so peculiar.
They wear artemisia to fill their belts,
Saying that fragrant orchids are not fit to be worn.
Their understanding of plants and trees is still lacking,
How can they appreciate the value of beautiful chéng gems?
They gather filth to stuff into their curtains,
Saying that *shēn jiāo* peppers are not fragrant.
I wanted to follow Líng Fēn's auspicious divination,
But my heart hesitated and was filled with doubt.
The shaman Wū Xián was about to descend in the evening,
I held *jiāo* pepper and offerings to meet him.
All the gods descended in full array,
The peaks of Jiǔ Yí welcomed them together.
The Sovereign shone brightly, displaying his divinity,
Telling me of auspicious reasons.
Saying, "Strive to rise and fall, going up and down,
Seeking where agreement can be found.
Tāng and Yǔ were strict in seeking harmony,
Zhì and Gāo Yáo were able to reconcile."
If your inner feelings truly love self-cultivation,
Then why is it necessary to employ matchmakers?
Yuè held a trowel and worked at Fù Yán,
Wǔ Dīng employed him without doubt.
Lǚ Wàng wielded a knife in Gǔ,
He encountered Zhōu Wén and was promoted.
Nìng Qī sang songs,
Qí Huán heard and comprehensively assisted him.
While the year is not yet late,
And time is still not yet halfway through.
I fear the early cry of the tíjué bird
, causing all the grasses to lose their fragrance.
Why do these jade pendants hang askew
, concealed from the crowd in shadow?
It is only that these partisans do not understand me
, I fear their jealousy will break me.
The times are chaotic and ever-changing
, how can I linger here?
The orchids and zhǐ plants have changed and lost their fragrance
, the quán and huì plants have transformed into thatch.
Why are the fragrant herbs of the past
now merely wormwood and artemisia?
Could there be another reason
? It is the harm of none cherishing cultivation.
I considered the orchid reliable
, but it is merely empty and grows tall.
It abandons its beauty to follow the vulgar
, merely to be listed among the many fragrant plants.
The pepper plant is flatteringly arrogant and careless
, and the shā plant also desires to fill the fragrant sachet.
Since they seek advancement and strive to enter
, how can fragrance be respected?
Indeed, the customs of the time flow and follow
, who can be without change?
Observing the pepper plants and orchids to be like this
, what more can be said of the jiēchē and jiānglí plants?
Only this pendant is precious
, abandoning its beauty to experience this.
The fragrant blossoms are luxuriant and hard to diminish,
their fragrance lingers even now.
I harmonize and modulate myself for enjoyment,
idly drifting and seeking a maiden.
While my adornments are at their finest,
I journey all around, observing high and low.
Líng Fēn has already given me an auspicious divination,
choosing a lucky day for my departure.
I break off jade branches as offerings,
refine jade flour as provisions.
For me, they harness flying dragons,
mixing precious jades and ivory to make my chariot.
How can those with differing hearts be together?
I shall depart far away to separate myself.
I turn my path towards Kūnlún,
the road long and winding as I journey around.
I raise the cloud banners, dim and obscure,
the jade bells on the carriage chime and chirp.
In the morning, I set off from Tiānjīn,
by evening, I arrive at the westernmost point.
The phoenixes assist in carrying the banners,
soaring high with graceful wings.
Suddenly, I travel through this shifting sand,
following the Red River and lingering leisurely.
I wave at the Jiaolong to make a bridge,
and command the Western Emperor (Xī Huáng) to ferry me across.
The road is long and full of hardship,
Have the mass of chariots take a shortcut and wait.
The road is incomplete and turns to the left,
Pointing to the Western Sea as the appointed time.
My chariots are stationed, a thousand strong,
With jade-decorated axles aligned and galloping side by side.
Driving eight dragons, gracefully winding,
Carrying cloud banners, undulating and long.
Suppressing my will and moderating my pace,
My spirit soars high, distantly far.
Playing the "Nine Songs" and dancing the "Shao,"
Briefly taking a day to steal some pleasure.
Ascending to the shining brilliance of the Emperor,
Suddenly looking down at my old home.
The coachman grieves, and my horses are homesick,
Crouching and looking back, refusing to move forward.
Finale:
Alas,
The country has no one who understands me,
Why should I long for the old capital?
Since no one is able to join me in creating beautiful government,
I will follow Peng Xián's place of dwelling.
Nine Songs
2.1 Dōng Huáng Tài Yī
On an auspicious day at a propitious time,
We shall reverently please the Supreme Emperor.
Stroking my long sword with jade-adorned hilts,
Qiúqiāng míng xī línláng. The jade pendants chime musically, a tinkling and clanging.
Yáo xí xī yù zhèn, Jade mats and jade pillows,
hé jiāng bǎ xī qióng fāng. Why not hold fragrant jade in our hands?
Huì yáo zhēng xī lán jí, Fragrant dishes steamed on mats of orchids,
diàn guì jiǔ xī jiāo jiāng. We offer cassia wine and peppered broth.
Yáng fú xī fǔ gǔ, Raise the drumsticks and strike the drums,
shū huǎn jié xī ān gē, With slow, relaxed rhythms, we sing peacefully,
chén yú sè xī hào chàng. We set out the yús and ses, singing loudly.
Líng yǎn jiǎn xī jiāo fú, The spirits move gracefully in beautiful attire,
fāng fēifēi xī mǎn táng. Fragrance fills the hall abundantly.
Wǔyīn fēn xī fán huì, The five tones mingle in complex harmony,
jūn xīnxīn xī lè kāng. The lord rejoices, happy and at peace.
2.2 Yúnzhōng Jūn The Lord in the Clouds
Yù lán tāng xī mù fāng, Bathed in orchid water, cleansed with fragrance,
huá cǎi yī xī ruò yīng. In splendid, colorful garments, like a flower.
Líng lián quán xī jì liú, The spirit lingers, curling and twisting,
làn zhāo zhāo xī wèi yāng. Shining brilliantly, without end.
Jiǎn jiāng dàn xī shòu gōng, I shall sojourn peacefully in the palace of longevity,
yǔ rì yuè xī qí guāng. Sharing radiance with the sun and moon.
Lóng jià xī dì fú, Dragon-drawn chariot and imperial garb,
liáo áo yóu xī zhōu zhāng. Let us wander and soar, touring all around.
Líng huáng huáng xī jì jiàng, The spirit descends in majestic glory,
biāo yuǎn jǔ xī yún zhōng. Whirls far away into the clouds.
Lǎn Jìzhōu xī yǒu yú, Gazing upon Jìzhōu with plenty to spare,
héng sì hǎi xī yān qióng. Crossing the four seas, where is the limit?
Sī fū jūn xī tàixī, Thinking of my lord, I sigh,
jí láo xīn xī pēngpēng. My heart is extremely troubled and agitated.
2.3 Xiāng Jūn The Lady of the Xiāng
Jūn bù xíng xī yíyóu, My lord does not come; he hesitates,
jiǎn shuí liú xī zhōng zhōu? For whom does he linger on the islet?
Měi yàomiǎo xī yí xiū, Beautiful and graceful, worthy of adornment,
pèi wú chéng xī guì zhōu. I harness my cassia boat.
I command the Yuán and Xiāng rivers to be without waves,
I cause the Jiāng river to flow calmly!
I gaze for my lord, but he does not come,
Playing the *c参cī* flute, whom do I think of!
Driving a flying dragon on a northern expedition,
I turn my path toward Lake Dòngtíng.
With creeping fig as curtains and sweet flag as hangings,
With *sūn* wood oars and orchid banners.
I gaze toward Cényáng, the farthest shore,
Crossing the great river, I raise my spirit.
Raising my spirit, but not to the limit,
The women, beautiful and graceful, sigh deeply for me.
Tears flow in a continuous stream,
Hidden thoughts of my lord cause me unease.
Cassia oar and orchid rudder,
Chopping ice and piling snow.
Gathering creeping fig in the water,
Plucking lotuses from the treetop.
Hearts not in accord, the go-between labors in vain,
Kindness not profound, easily broken off.
The rocky rapids are shallow,
The flying dragon soars gracefully.
Making friends without loyalty leads to lasting resentment;
Promising without sincerity, yet telling me you're not free!
In the morning, I gallop wildly along the riverbank,
In the evening, I halt my horse by the northern islet.
Birds perch upon the rooftops,
Water encircles the hall below.
I cast my jade ring into the river,
I leave my pendant in Lǐ Pǔ.
I gather dùruò orchids on the fragrant islet,
Intending to give them to the serving girls.
Time cannot be regained,
So let me wander freely and at ease.
2.4 The Xiāng Fūren (Lady of the Xiang)
The Emperor's daughter descends to the northern islet,
My eyes, gazing into the distance, are filled with sorrow.
Softly blows the autumn wind,
The waves of Dòngtíng and falling leaves of the trees.
I gaze afar from the white bái fán,
A rendezvous with my love is set for the evening.
Birds gather in the duckweed,
Why is the fishing net on the tree?
In the Yuán River there are zhǐ, and in Lǐ there are orchids.
I long for the prince, but dare not speak.
Vaguely, I gaze into the distance,
Watching the flowing water gurgle.
What do the deer eat in the courtyard?
What do the dragons do on the water's edge?
I race my remaining horse along the riverbank in the morning,
And cross to the western shore in the evening.
I hear that the beautiful woman is summoning me,
I will prepare my chariot and depart together.
I build a house in the water,
And thatch it with lotus leaves.
Walls of *sūn* grass and a purple altar,
I scatter fragrant peppers to form a hall.
Cinnamon pillars and orchid rafters,
Magnolia lintels and rooms of medicinal herbs.
I spread *bìlì* creeper as curtains,
And part the *huì mián* reeds already stretched.
White jade as weights,
And scattered *shílán* orchids for fragrance.
I thatch the lotus house with *zhǐ* grass,
And surround it with *dùhéng*.
I gather a hundred herbs to fill the courtyard,
And build fragrant verandas at the gate.
The Jiǔyí mountains are colorful and come to greet us together,
The spirits come like clouds.
I throw my sleeve into the river,
And leave my undergarment on the Lǐpǔ shore.
I pluck *dùruò* on the islet,
To give to the one far away.
The time is not right to quickly obtain her,
So I leisurely ramble in ease.
2.5 Dà Sīmìng (The Great Master of Fate)
Widen wide, oh, the Heavenly Gate,
In multitudes I ride, oh, on dark clouds.
I order the whirlwind to be my vanguard,
I send the pouring rain to sprinkle dust.
My lord circles and descends,
He crosses the empty mulberry tree to follow me.
In bustling crowds, oh, throughout the nine provinces,
Why is long life or premature death in my hands?
I fly high and soar in peace,
Riding on pure Qi, controlling Yin and Yang.
I and my lord abstain and purify ourselves quickly,
Guiding the Di through the nine hollows.
My divine garments are flowing and layered,
My jade pendants dangle and shimmer.
Once Yin, once Yang,
The masses do not know what I do.
I break off coarse hemp and beautiful flowers,
I will use them to present to the separated ones.
Old age creeps on slowly and is approaching its limit,
Not gradually nearing, but growing increasingly distant.
Riding dragons, oh, rumbling along,
Towering high, oh, soaring to the heavens.
I tie together cassia branches and wait longingly,
How greatly I think of the sorrowful person!
Sorrowful person, oh, what to do?
I wish to be like this now, without loss.
Truly, human life has its fate,
Who can decide separation or reunion?
2.6 Shǎo Sīmìng
Autumn orchids and *míwú* grasses,
Growing in rows beneath the hall.
Green leaves and white branches,
Fragrant and lush, they assail me.
The Lady surely has her beautiful child,
Why then is Sūn so sorrowful?
Autumn orchids, how verdant,
Green leaves and purple stems.
The hall is full of beauties,
Suddenly, her eyes meet mine alone.
Entering without a word, leaving without a farewell,
Riding the whirlwind, bearing cloud banners.
Nothing is more sorrowful than parting while still alive,
Nothing is more joyful than a new acquaintance.
Dressed in lotus, belted with sweetflag,
Swiftly she comes, suddenly she departs.
At dusk she lodges on the Emperor’s outskirts,
Whom do you await at the edge of the clouds?
I wander with you by the Nine Rivers,
A rushing wind arrives, and the water raises waves.
I bathe with you in the Salt Pool,
I dry your hair on the sunny bank.
I gaze, awaiting the beauty who has not come,
Facing the wind, in a daze, I sing aloud.
With a parasol and green pennants,
Ascending the nine heavens, stroking the comet.
Holding aloft my long sword, embracing the young *ài*,
Sūn is uniquely suited to be upright for the people.
2.7 The Lord of the East
The sun is about to rise in the east,
Shining on my railing, the Fusang tree.
I stroke my horse, driving it slowly,
The night was bright, now it is dawn.
Driving a dragon chariot, riding on thunder,
Carrying cloud banners that undulate.
I sigh deeply, about to ascend,
My heart lingering, looking back with longing.
The Qiāng music and sights delight the people,
The viewers are calm and forget to return.
Tightening the zither strings, interlacing the drums,
Flutes and bells on jeweled stands,
Playing the chí flute, blowing the yú reed organ,
I think of the spirit intermediaries, so virtuous and beautiful.
Swiftly flying, like kingfisher feathers layered,
Unfolding poems, gathering for dance.
Responding to the rhythms, matching the beats,
The arrival of the spirit obscures the sun.
Wearing clothes of green clouds and a skirt of white rainbow,
Raising a long arrow, I shoot the Sirius star.
Grasping my bow, I turn and descend,
Lifting the Big Dipper, I ladle out cinnamon wine.
Taking up my reins, I soar high,
Into the dim distance, I travel east.
2.8 The River God
traveled with a woman on the nine rivers,
a strong wind arose, and waves spread horizontally.
Riding a water chariot and holding a lotus canopy,
driving two dragons and flanking them with chī dragons.
Ascending Mount Kūnlún and gazing in all directions,
my heart soared, vast and unrestrained.
As the sun was setting, I felt lost and forgot to return,
only at the far shore did I awaken with longing.
Fish-scale houses and dragon halls,
purple seashell gates and vermilion palaces.
What is the spirit doing in the water?
Riding a white turtle and chasing patterned fish.
Traveling with a woman on the river's islet,
melting ice flows are swirling and about to come down.
You held my hand and went east,
escorting the beauty to the southern shore.
The waves surged to welcome us,
the fish, in close ranks, accompanied me.
2.9 The Mountain Spirit
It seems there is someone on the mountainside,
draped in creeping fig and girdled with dodder.
Already holding a lingering gaze, and also fitting to smile,
you admire me for my graceful figure.
Riding a red leopard and followed by patterned wildcats,
with a magnolia chariot and a cassia banner fastened.
Draped in rock orchids and girdled with Chinese wild ginger,
I pluck fragrant blossoms to give to the one I long for.
I dwell amongst secluded bamboo groves, never seeing the sky.
The path is treacherous and difficult, and I alone am late in arriving.
I stand alone atop the mountain,
Where the clouds billow gently below.
In the deep darkness, even the daytime seems obscure.
The east wind blows, and a divine rain falls.
I linger for the beautiful one, calmly forgetting to return home.
The year is late; who will adorn me with flowers?
I gather the three auspicious plants amidst the mountains,
Where the rocks are piled high, and the kudzu vines spread.
I resent the young lord, sadly forgetting to return home.
My lord thinks of me, but has no leisure.
I am a mountain dweller who is like fragrant *dùruò*.
I drink from the stone springs and find shade under the pines and cypresses.
My lord thinks of me, yet suspicion arises.
The thunder rumbles, and the rain falls heavily.
The monkeys screech, and the night cries again.
The wind rustles, and the trees sigh.
Thinking of the young lord, I only increase my sorrows.
2.10 *Guó Shāng* (Elegy for the Fallen)
We grasp Wu spears and don rhinoceros armor.
Chariot wheels clash as we engage in close combat.
Banners blot out the sun, and the enemy is like clouds.
Arrows fall in a dense rain as our soldiers fight to be first.
They overrun our ranks and trample our lines; they trample and overrun our lines.
The left charioteer is slain, and the right one is wounded by a blade.
I restrain two wheels with four horses,
I grasp the jade drumstick and strike the resounding drum.
The season of heaven descends, and majestic spirits are enraged,
Harsh slaughter is complete, abandoning the open fields.
Going out never to return, going forth never to come back,
The plains are vast, the road exceedingly far.
Wearing a long sword, carrying a Qín bow,
Though head and body are separated, the heart does not repent.
Truly brave, and also martial,
Ultimately strong and unyielding, and cannot be insulted.
Now that the body is dead, the spirit lives on,
May your soul and spirit become a hero among ghosts.
2.11 *Lǐ Hún* (Summoning the Soul with Ritual)
The ritual is complete, the drums gather,
Passing *bā*, dancing in turn,
Beautiful women sing, gracefully and leisurely.
Spring orchids and autumn chrysanthemums,
May they never cease, lasting forever.

A shepherd from Yǒu Hù,

In darkness and secrecy, he followed traces,

Dào jī Zhòu gōng, He arrived and struck Zhòu's body,

zú, this matter,

how was its position established?

Gǔ dāo yáng shēng, He beat the knife and raised his voice,

*Jiǔ Zhāng*
4.1 *Xī Sòng*
I regret reciting, leading to sorrow,
I express my indignation to pour out my feelings.
What I compose is loyal and I speak of it,
I point to the azure sky to attest to its correctness.
I order the Five Emperors to mediate with fairness,
I warn the Six Gods to be obedient.
I commission the mountains and rivers to prepare for defense,
I command Gāo Yáo to listen to the right.
I exhaust my loyalty to serve my lord,
Yet I am alienated from the group and considered a superfluous growth.
I forget flattery to turn my back on the multitude,
Awaiting a wise ruler to understand me.
My words and deeds, they are traceable,
My feelings and appearance, they do not change.
Therefore, a minister cannot be more devoted than to his ruler,
So the proof of this is not far off.
I prioritize my duty to the ruler over myself,
But this is what the multitude hates.
I focus solely on the ruler without other considerations,
And yet this is what the myriad people resent.
With a single-minded focus and without hesitation,
Alas, it is not sustainable.
I hate those who are close to the ruler and have no other purpose,
This is a path that invites disaster.
Thinking of my lord, could it be that I am not loyal?
I suddenly forget my humble and impoverished state.
Serving my lord without duplicity,
I am confused and unaware of the path to favor.
What crime is loyalty, that it meets with punishment?
It is not what my heart desires.
Acting differently from the crowd and being unconventional,
I am derided by the multitude.
Encountering accusations and slanders in abundance,
it is difficult to explain.
My feelings are suppressed and cannot be expressed,
and they are obscured, and no one vindicates me.
My heart is distressed and forlorn,
and no one understands my inner feelings.
Indeed, tiresome words cannot fully convey my meaning,
I wish to express my intentions, but there is no way.
I withdraw into silence, but no one understands me,
I advance and cry out, but no one hears me.
I repeat my distress and confusion,
my heart is heavy with stifled emotions.
Once, I dreamed of ascending to heaven,
but my soul lost its way in the middle of the journey.
I had the Lí shén (a spirit) divine it,
and he said that my aspirations were extreme and had no boundaries.
In the end, I stand alone in danger and alienation,
and it is said that the ruler can be thought of, but not relied upon.
Therefore, the mouths of the multitude can melt metal;
at first it seems like this, but one encounters danger.
One who has learned a lesson from hot soup blows on cold vegetables;
why not change this mindset?
To want to abandon the stairs and climb to heaven,
is still like the old habit.
The crowd is frightened and alienated,
so how can you make them your companions?
Reaching the same end by different paths,
how can you make them your helpers?
Jìn Shēnshēng 晉申生 was a filial son;
his father believed slander and did not approve of him.
He acted stubbornly and honestly but was not indulged;
Gǔn 鯀 accomplished his task but did not succeed.
I have heard that doing one's duty creates resentment;
one suddenly calls it a mistake.
After breaking an arm many times, one becomes a doctor;
I now know that it is truly so.
The arrow trap is set above;
the nets are spread below.
Setting out Zhang Pì 張辟 to please the ruler,
I wish to withdraw myself and have nowhere to go.
Wanting to drift about and wait for distress,
I fear accumulating troubles and incurring blame.
Wanting to fly high and gather far away,
the ruler may ask, "Where do you think you are going?"
Wanting to flee wildly and lose my way,
Firm in resolve, yet lacking in forbearance.
My back and chest feel the sharp pain of separation,
My heart is oppressed, knotted, and twisted with worry.
I falsely attribute magnolia's goodness to cassia,
And use wild pepper to satisfy my hunger.
I plant Jiāng Lí and cultivate chrysanthemums,
Hoping for spring days to provide fragrant dried provisions.
I fear my true feelings will not be believed,
Therefore, I repeatedly write to clarify myself.
I suppress this beauty for private dwelling,
Wishing for continued thought and distance from the body.
4.2 Shè Jiāng (Crossing the River)
From youth, I loved these strange garments,
Now old, I have not declined.
I wear a long sword with its glittering,
And a tall hat that touches the clouds.
I am draped in moonlight and wear jade pendants.
The world is turbid and no one understands me,
I gallop onward without looking back.
I drive a blue dragon and harness white chī,
I travel with Chóng Huá to the Yáo garden.
I ascend Kūnlún and eat jade essence,
To share longevity with Heaven and Earth,
And share radiance with the sun and moon.
I grieve that the southern barbarians do not understand me,
At dawn, I cross the Jiāng and Xiāng rivers.
I ride along the banks of È Zhǔ and look back,
Sighing at the initial winds of autumn and winter.
I walk my horse on the hillsides,
And park my carriage in the dense forest.
I board a light boat and sail up the Yuán River,
And urge the rowers on with unified strokes to strike the waves.
The boat lingers and does not advance,
Hesitating in the swirling waters, doubting and stalling.
In the morning, I set out from Wǎng Zhǔ,
And in the evening, I lodge at Chén Yáng.
If only my heart is upright and honest,
What harm is there in being remote and distant?
Entering the Xù Pǔ marsh, I linger aimlessly,
Lost and not knowing where I am going.
The deep forest is dim and dark,
A place where monkeys and gibbons dwell.
The mountains are steep and high, blocking the sun,
Below is dark and gloomy, with much rain.
Sleet and snow fall endlessly,
Clouds drift and fill the sky.
I grieve for the lack of joy in my life,
Living alone in the mountains.
I cannot change my heart to follow the vulgar customs,
Surely I will face sorrow and bitterness until my end.
Jiē Yú shaved his head,
Sāng Hù roamed naked.
Loyalty is not necessarily employed,
and talent is not necessarily used.
Wǔ Zǐ 胥 met with disaster,
Bǐ Gān was minced and pickled.
Since it has always been so in previous ages,
why should I resent the people of today!
I will uphold the Way without hesitation,
and I am determined to spend my life in deep darkness!
Envoi:
The *luán* bird and the phoenix are growing more distant each day.
Swallows and magpies nest in halls and on altars.
Lù Shēn and Xīn Yí die in thickets.
The foul and fetid are placed side by side; fragrance cannot approach.
Yin and Yang have exchanged places; the time is not right.
Cherishing faith and feeling lost,
suddenly, I am about to depart!
4.3 Lament for Yǐng
August Heaven's decrees are not constant;
why is the common people's transgression so severe?
The people are scattered and separated,
and in the middle of spring, they are moving eastward.
Leaving their old homes and going to a distant place,
they follow the Jiāng and Xià Rivers in exile.
Leaving the city gates and feeling heavy-hearted,
they set out on the day *jiǎ* of the month *cháo wú*.
Departing from Yǐngdū and leaving the lane,
where will it all end in this vast emptiness?
The oars are raised in unison, proceeding slowly,
I lament seeing my lord and being unable to see him again.
I gaze at the tall *qiū* trees and sigh,
My tears fall like sleet.
Passing Xiàshǒu and floating westward,
I look back at Lóngmén, but it is nowhere to be seen.
My heart is unsettled and grieved,
Vaguely, I know not where to tread.
Following the wind and waves, I drift along,
Wandering aimlessly, becoming a traveler.
Surmounting the vastness of Yáng Hóu's domain,
Suddenly soaring aloft, where to alight?
My heart is entangled and cannot be freed,
My thoughts are frustrated and cannot be released.
I will steer the boat and float downstream,
From the upper Dòngtíng Lake down the river.
Leaving the place where I dwelt of old,
Now, leisurely, I come eastward.
Oh, my spirit desires to return,
How can it forget to return even for a moment?
Leaving Xiàpǔ and thinking westward,
I grieve that the old capital is growing more distant each day.
Ascending a large mound, I gaze into the distance,
Hoping to ease my troubled heart.
I lament the peace and joy of my state,
I mourn the enduring customs of the river borders.
Where will I arrive when I reach Língyáng?
How will I cross south across the vast expanse?
I never knew that the summer palace would become a ruin,
who would have thought that the two gates east of the city could become overgrown with weeds?
My heart is not happy for long,
worry and sorrow follow each other.
The road to Yǐng is so far,
the Jiāng River and the Xià River are impossible to cross.
It is as if I do not believe it,
yet nine years have passed and I have not returned.
How sad and stifled, unable to break through,
stumbling and hesitating, harboring sorrow!
Outwardly, I strive to please with grace,
but I am really weak and hard to support.
My loyalty is pure and I wish to advance,
but jealousy causes me to be alienated and blocked.
Yáo and Shùn acted with integrity,
their virtue reached far and wide and approached heaven.
But the jealous multitude slandered them,
falsely accusing them of being unkind.
They hated and resented their cultivated beauty,
and favored the noblewoman's arrogance.
The crowd stumbled forward day by day,
while virtue was surpassed and left behind.
Luan (envoi):
I let my eyes wander and gaze afar,
hoping for a chance to return; when will it be?
Birds fly back to their old homes,
foxes die turning their heads toward their mounds.
I was abandoned and banished, but it was not my fault.
How can I forget it day and night?
4.4 Drawing Thoughts
My heart is filled with brooding sorrow,
I sigh alone, increasing my grief.
My thoughts are troubled and cannot be released,
and I am overwhelmed by the long night.
I am saddened by the autumn wind that stirs the features of my face,
how confusedly it turns and floats.
It is because Sūn is so easily angered,
that my heart is wounded and sorrowful.
I wish to shake myself up and rush away,
to examine the faults of the people and calm myself.
I gather my slight feelings to present my words,
and haughtily leave them to that beauty.
In the past, you spoke sincerely to me,
saying that we would meet at dusk.
But you turned back halfway,
and changed your mind.
You acted arrogantly because of your beauty,
and looked at me because of my fine appearance.
You spoke to me but did not believe me,
and purposely created anger towards me.
I wish to take advantage of a moment to examine myself,
but my heart trembles with grief and I dare not.
I sadly hesitate and hope to advance,
but my heart is wearied with empty grief.
Now I painstakingly present my case,
but my lord seems deaf and hears nothing.
It is because I am truthful and do not flatter that,
the multitude indeed considers me a calamity.
Initially, my counsel was clearly evident,
how could it be useless and forgotten now?
Why are my earnest words like bitter medicine?
I wish that my lord's virtue could be complete.
I look to the example of Sān Wǔ (the Three Kings and Five Emperors),
and point to Péng Xián as a model.
What limit is there that one cannot reach?
Therefore, my distant reputation is difficult to tarnish.
Goodness does not come from external sources,
reputation cannot be falsely made.
Who can receive rewards without giving?
Who can harvest without planting?
A short song says:
I draw out my grievances with a beautiful person,
spending days and nights without resolution.
She is arrogant because of her beauty,
and haughtily rejects my words, refusing to listen.
A song says:
There is a bird from the south,
that comes to gather in the north of the Hàn River.
It is beautiful and elegant,
but lives alone in this foreign land.
Already being lonely and isolated,
Moreover, there is no good matchmaker by her side.
The path is lofty and distant, and days are forgotten;
I wish to express myself, but cannot.
Looking towards Běi Shān (North Mountain), I shed tears;
Standing by the flowing water, I deeply sigh!
Gazing upon the short nights of early summer,
Why does the alternation of darkness and light seem like a year?
The road to Yǐng (郢) is so long and far,
My soul departs nine times in a single night.
I do not even know whether the road is winding or straight;
I point southward to the moon and the array of stars.
I wish to quickly depart but cannot,
My soul's consciousness is anxiously searching for the road.
How truthful and straightforward is my spirit!
People's hearts do not agree with my own!
My reasoning is weak and the matchmaker does not communicate,
They still do not understand my composure.
Finale:
The long rapid flows swiftly, ascending to the river's depths.
Madly looking around, I travel south, just to entertain my heart.
The piled-up rocks are steep and perilous, thwarting my desires.
Surpassing, turning back, and measuring intentions, I proceed obscurely and cautiously.
Lingering and hesitating, I lodge at Běi Gū (北姑).
Vexed, grieved, and confused, indeed I rush to leave.
Sorrowfully sighing, grieving my spirit, my soul thinks from afar.
The road is far, the place secluded, and there is no one to act as a go-between.
When the way of thinking produces a song, I temporarily rescue myself.
My worried heart's desires unfulfilled, to whom can I tell this?
4.5 Huái Shā (Embracing Sand)
In the overflowing early summer,
the grasses and trees are luxuriant.
Grieving with lasting sorrow,
I drift away towards the southern lands.
Dimly, ah, far away,
all is still, quiet, and silent.
My feelings are knotted and twisting,
departing with sorrow, I nurture myself for a long time.
I control my feelings to follow my will,
wronged, yet restraining myself.
To carve the square into a circle,
a constant standard that cannot be changed.
To change what was initially correct,
is despised by the superior man.
To clearly delineate intentions with ink,
means the previous plan has not been altered.
With inner substance and upright character,
the great man esteems this.
Even if Qiǎo Chuí (巧倕) does not carve,
who can discern his correcting what is wrong?
Dark patterns in a hidden place,
the blind call them unadorned;
even if Lí Lóu (離婁) subtly glances,
A blind man thinks there is no light.
He mistakes white for black,
And turns up into down.
The fènghuáng is in a cage,
While chickens and ducks soar and dance.
Jade and stone are mixed together,
And measured with the same standard.
It is only that the cliques are base and narrow-minded,
That they simply do not know what I value.
Entrusted with heavy burdens and great responsibilities,
I am mired down and cannot succeed.
Holding jade and grasping precious stones,
I am impoverished and cannot show them.
The village dogs bark in packs,
Barking at what they find strange.
They suspect the outstanding and doubt the exceptional;
Indeed, that is the way of the mediocre.
My cultivated qualities are subtly concealed within,
So the masses do not know of my extraordinary talents.
My unadorned abilities are piled up,
But no one knows what I possess.
I value benevolence and uphold righteousness,
And cautiously consider sincerity to be abundance.
[Chóng Huá] is too distant to reach,
Who knows of my composure!
From ancient times, things have not existed side by side,
How can one know the reason why?
Tāng Yǔ is long past,
so distant and unattainable.
I restrain my lingering anger and change my resentment,
suppressing my heart and forcing myself to be strong.
Separated from the sympathetic and unmoving,
I hope my will can be embodied.
Proceeding north along the road,
the sun is dimly sinking towards dusk.
I release my worries and find joy in sorrow,
bound by a great purpose.
Finale:
Vast are the Yuán and Xiāng rivers, their currents swirling.
The long road is hidden and obscure, the way is distant and indistinct.
Cherishing my virtue and embracing my feelings, I am uniquely unmatched.
Bólè is already gone, where can a Jì be judged?
The lives of all people have their place.
With a determined heart and broad ambitions, what have I to fear?
Once wounded and saddened, I sigh eternally.
The world is turbid and no one knows me,
the human heart is unpredictable.
Knowing that death cannot be avoided,
I wish not to cherish life.
I clearly tell noble men,
I will take you as my companions.
4.6 *Sī Měirén* (Thinking of the Beautiful One)
Thinking of the beautiful one,
I wipe away tears and stand gazing.
The matchmaker is cut off, the road is blocked,
words cannot be tied together and conveyed.
The earnestness of my vexed grievance,
is trapped and cannot be expressed.
I extend the day to ease my inner feelings,
my will is sunk and concealed, but cannot be understood.
I wish to entrust my words to the floating clouds,
but encounter Fēnglóng who will not deliver them.
I rely on the returning birds to send my message,
but they roost so high, it is difficult to reach them.
The spiritual prosperity of Gāo Xīn,
encountered the dark bird who delivered the message.
I want to change my principles to follow customs,
but I am ashamed to change my original intent and bend my will.
I have experienced years of grief and sorrow alone,
but my heart still hasn't changed.
I would rather conceal my sorrows and live a long life,
why would I make such a change?
Knowing that the previous path was unsuccessful,
I have not changed this measure.
The cart has overturned and the horse has stumbled,
I alone cherish this different path.
I rein in the excellent steed and change the carriage,
Zàofù will drive it for me.
Let it retreat and proceed slowly and do not rush it,
let us temporarily take a day off to wait for the right time.
I point to the western bend of Mount Bōzhǒng,
And with dark red and yellow I made my tryst.
As spring unfolds and the year begins anew,
The white sun emerges leisurely.
I shall give free rein to my will and find joy,
Following the Jiāngxià River to dispel my sorrows.
I gather fragrant zhǐ (芷) from the great thickets,
And pluck withered plants from the long islet.
I lament that I cannot be like the ancients,
With whom shall I enjoy these fragrant herbs?
I undo the biǎnbó (萹薄) and mixed vegetables,
Preparing them as interwoven pendants.
The pendants are colorful and twirling,
But soon they wither, break, and separate.
I shall linger and stroll to amuse my sorrows,
Observing the changes of the Southern people.
Secret joy is in my heart,
Letting out that which relies on me without delay.
Fragrance and moisture are intermingled,
Yet the fragrance of the flowers issues forth from within.
Luxuriantly they extend afar,
Filling the interior and spreading outward.
Emotion and substance can surely be preserved,
Though hidden, their pattern is heard.
To use *bìlì* (薜荔) as a guide,
I fear to lift my foot and climb the trees.
Because of the lotus, I act as a matchmaker,
I dread lifting my skirt and wetting my feet.
Climbing high is not to my liking,
Descending low I cannot do.
Indeed, my form is unsuited to this,
So I hesitate and remain in doubt.
To broadly carry out the previous plan,
I have not changed this intention.
If fate dictates I dwell in obscurity, I will cease my efforts,
Wishing to do so before the white sun has set.
Alone and desolate, I travel south,
Thinking of the example of Péng Xián.
4.7 Regretting the Past
I regret that in the past I was trusted,
Receiving orders and using illustrious poems to make pronouncements.
Serving the accomplishments of my predecessors to illuminate those below,
Clarifying doubts about laws and regulations.
The state was rich and powerful, and the laws were established,
Relying on loyal ministers, but jealousy grew daily.
Secret matters were carried in my heart,
Even mistakes were not corrected.
My heart was pure and expansive and did not reveal secrets,
But I encountered slanderers who envied me.
The ruler held anger and waited for his minister to act,
Without clearly investigating the truth.
Obscuring the ruler's clear perception,
Vain illusions were used to deceive him further.
Without cross-referencing to verify the facts,
He banished loyal subjects afar and did not think [of it].
Believing in the filth and turbidity of slanderous flatterers,
He swelled with arrogance and overdid it.
Why were loyal ministers without fault,
Yet slandered and blamed?
Ashamed of the honesty and trustworthiness of the sun and moon,
I hid myself in seclusion, preparing for the worst.
Approaching the dark depths of the Yuán and Xiāng Rivers,
I then resigned myself and plunged into the flow.
Finally, I lost my life and my name was cut off,
Regretting that I could not enlighten the sovereign.
The sovereign was without measure and did not observe,
Causing fragrant herbs to become hidden in thickets.
How could I express my feelings and reveal my sincerity,
Peaceful in death and without comfort?
Uniquely blocked and obscured,
Causing loyal ministers to be without recourse.
I have heard that Bǎilǐ was a captive,
Yī Yǐn was a cook in the kitchen.
Lǚ Wàng was a butcher in Zhāogē,
Níng Qī sang while feeding oxen.
If they had not met Tāng, Wǔ, and Huán Mù,
Who in the world would have spoken of them and known them?
Wú believed slander and did not heed it,
Zǐ Xū died and then he worried.
Jiè Zǐ was loyal and stood until he withered,
Duke Wén awoke and sought him out.
Sealing Jièshān and forbidding access to it,
Repaying great virtue with leisurely wandering.
Thinking of old loyal acquaintances personally,
Because of the white silk, I weep for them.
Some are loyal and die for their principles,
Others are deceitful and not doubted.
Not examining and verifying the facts,
Listening to the false words of slanderers.
Fragrant and foul are mixed together,
Who will distinguish them in the daylight?
Why do fragrant herbs wither so early?
When even light frost falls, they don't heed the warning.
Truly, hearing is obscured and blocked,
Allowing slander and flattery to prevail daily.
Since past generations have envied the worthy,
They say *huì* and *ruò* are unworthy of being worn.
Jealous of the fragrance of beautiful people,
Mó Mǔ thinks herself beautiful and self-satisfied.
Though there is Xī Shī’s beauty,
Slander and jealousy creep in to take her place.
Wishing to express my feelings to clear my conduct,
I unexpectedly committed a transgression.
The injustice will be seen in the light of day,
Like stars misplaced in the sky.
Riding a *qílì* horse and galloping,
Without reins or bit, it carries itself;
Riding a raft downstream,
Without boats or oars prepared.
Turning one's back on laws and measures while desiring orderly governance
Is no different from turning aside.
I would rather die swiftly and drift away,
Than fear calamity might strike again.
Not finishing my words, I rush into the abyss,
Regretting the sovereign's lack of understanding.
4.8 *Jú Sòng* (Ode to the Orange)
The august and excellent tree, the orange, came to serve.
Receiving its destiny, it does not move, born in the southern land.
Deeply rooted and difficult to transplant, it changes only in purpose.
Green leaves and white blossoms, how pleasingly abundant!
Slender branches with sharp thorns, round fruits clustered together.
Green and yellow mingled, the patterns are radiant.
Pure color inside white, it is surely fit for responsibility.
A profusion of flavors suitable for cultivation, beautiful and not ugly.
Ah, your youthful aspiration is uniquely different.
Standing alone and unmoving, how can you not be admired?
Deeply rooted and difficult to transplant, you are expansive and without desire.
Standing independent and aloof from the world, upright and not drifting along.
Guarding your heart and being cautious, you will not ultimately make mistakes.
Upholding virtue without selfishness, you are in accord with Heaven and Earth.
I wish to wither away with the years, and be a long-time friend with you.
Excellent, yet not excessive, principled and having reason.
Though young in years, you can be a teacher and leader.
Your conduct is like that of Bó Yí, let us set you up as an example.
4.9 "Bēi Huí Fēng"
"Bēi Huí Fēng" sways the fragrant orchids,
My heart is knotted with grievances, wounded within.
Things, though small, can lose their nature,
Sounds, though faint, are the first to rise.
Why did Péng Xián conceive such thoughts,
And maintain his integrity without forgetting?
Myriad changes of feeling cannot be concealed;
What falsehood can endure?
Birds and beasts cry out to gather their flocks,
Coarse plants gather but are not fragrant.
Fish cover their scales to distinguish themselves,
While dragons conceal their patterns.
Therefore, bitter herbs and fragrant plants are not in the same field,
Orchids and irises are secluded and uniquely fragrant.
Only a beautiful person dwells forever in the capital,
Inheriting the world and bestowing upon themselves.
Far-reaching are the limits of their ambition,
Pitying the aimless wandering of floating clouds.
Confused are the limits of their ambition,
Secretly expressing what poetry can make clear.
Only the beautiful person cherishes these thoughts alone,
Breaking off young pepper branches to find solace.
Often sighing with tears and lamentations,
Hidden and brooding in solitude.
Tears mingle and fall sadly,
Thinking sleeplessly until dawn.
The long night stretches out endlessly,
Concealing this sorrow that will not depart.
I wake leisurely and wander around,
Briefly finding ease to rely on myself.
Wounded by sighs of pity and compassion,
The breath gathers in my throat and cannot be stopped.
I twist my thoughts into a sash,
And weave my sorrows into a breastplate.
I break off a branch of the Ruò mù tree to shield the light,
And follow where the whirlwind carries me.
I cling to vague impressions but cannot see clearly,
My heart leaps and throbs like boiling water.
I stroke my sash and adjust my robe to calm my spirit,
And with a feeling of being lost, I then proceed.
The years pass swiftly as if collapsing,
And time too will gradually arrive.
The Fén héng grasses wither and their joints separate,
Their fragrance fades and they are no longer comparable.
I pity my heart, which cannot be restrained from longing,
Proving that these words cannot offer comfort.
I would rather die and drift away,
Than endure this constant sorrow.
The orphaned son sobs and wipes away his tears,
The exiled son goes forth and does not return.
Who can think without concealing their thoughts,
Illuminating what Péng Xián heard?
Ascending the rocky peak to gaze afar,
The road stretches afar in silent obscurity.
Entering a landscape where echoes find no response,
Hearing and reflecting become unattainable.
Sorrow wells up, unrelieved,
Dwelling in unease, with no solution.
The heart is bridled and cannot express itself,
The breath coils and binds itself.
The deep distance stretches endlessly,
The vast wilderness has no bounds.
Sounds have a hidden sympathy,
Things have a purity that cannot be fabricated.
Dimly spreading, immeasurable,
Faintly continuous, unyielding.
Sorrow quietly remains, a constant grief,
Lightly obscure, incapable of amusement.
I ride the great waves and floating winds,
Trusting in the dwelling place of Péng Xián.
Climbing the steep banks of high cliffs,
Residing on the summit of the female rainbow.
Grasping the blue sky, I unfurl the rainbow,
Suddenly grasping, I touch the heavens.
I suck the floating source of glistening dew,
Rinse my mouth with the abundant frozen frost.
I rest in the wind cave,
Suddenly waking, I stretch and sigh.
Leaning on Kūnlún to overlook the mists,
Concealing myself in Mínshān to purify the Jiāng River.
I dread the rushing torrents crashing,
listening to the booming sound of the waves.
The appearance is disorderly and without measure,
vague and boundless, without any record.
The expanse is vast, with no way to follow,
and drifting changes, where will they stop?
Tossed about, swirling up and down,
soaring far and wide to the left and right.
Flooding torrents before and behind,
accompanying the ebb and flow of the tide.
I observe the heat of the sun following,
and I peer into where the mists accumulate.
I lament the simultaneous descent of frost and snow,
and I listen to the colliding of the tides.
I borrow the light to go back and forth,
and apply the yellow thorns as crooked divining stalks.
I seek the place where Jiè Zǐ 介子 dwells,
and I see the abandoned traces of Bó Yí 伯夷.
My heart is tempered and does not depart,
engraving my will without shifting.
I say:
I resent what I hoped for in the past,
and I grieve for the anxious future.
I float from the Jiāng 淮 River and enter the sea,
following Zǐ Xū 子胥 and finding contentment.
I gaze upon the islands and shores of the great river,
and I lament the steadfast tracks of Shēn Tū 申徒.
I earnestly advised the ruler, but he would not listen;
What good is it to heavily burden Shí (石)?
My heart is entangled and cannot be untied;
My thoughts are troubled and cannot be released.
Yuǎnyóu (遠遊)
I grieve for the oppression of the times and customs;
I wish to lightly ascend and travel far away.
My substance is meager and without means;
Where shall I entrust myself to ride and float upwards?
Encountering turbidity and becoming sullied;
Alone, I am depressed and to whom can I speak!
The night is brightly sleepless;
My soul is isolated and reaches dawn.
Only the Heaven and Earth are without end;
I grieve for the long toil of human life.
The past, I cannot reach;
The future, I have not heard of.
I pace back and forth, thinking from afar;
Disappointed and disoriented, I deviate from my intentions.
My thoughts are vague and wandering;
My heart is filled with sorrow and increases my grief.
My spirit suddenly departs and does not return;
My body is withered and remains alone.
Inwardly, I examine myself to maintain proper conduct;
Seeking the source of righteous qi.
Silently empty and still, I am tranquil and pleased;
Remaining tranquil in non-action and attaining self-satisfaction.
Hearing of the pure dust of Chì Sōng (赤松),
I wish to inherit his legacy.
Valuing the excellent virtue of the true person,
Praising the past generations who ascended to immortality.
They departed with transformation and are no longer seen,
But their reputation is renowned and grows daily.
Marveling at Fù Yuè’s (傅說) entrustment to the Morning Star,
Envying Hán Zhòng’s (韓眾) attainment of unity,
Their form became increasingly distant,
Separating from the crowd and escaping.
Relying on the changes of Qi, they then soared,
Suddenly like divine runners and ghostly wonders.
At times they vaguely appear from afar,
Their essence bright and constantly returning.
Separating from the dust and purifying the extraordinary,
They never return to their former capital.
Freed from all misfortunes and without fear,
The world does not know where they have gone.
Fearing the sequential order of the seasons,
Yàolíng (耀靈, the sun) shines brightly and heads west.
A light frost descends and the world sinks down,
Grieving for the early withering of the fragrant grasses.
I shall wander about and be carefree,
Passing through years without accomplishment.
Who can I share this lingering fragrance with?
In the morning, I release my emotions to the wind.
Gāoyáng (高陽) is distant and remote,
where shall I proceed?
Chóng (重) says:
Spring and autumn swiftly pass and do not linger,
why stay long in this old dwelling?
Xuānyuán (軒轅) is beyond reach,
I shall follow Wáng Qiáo (王喬) and find amusement!
I eat the six qi and drink the dew of the heavens,
rinse my mouth with the pure yang and hold the morning glow.
I preserve the clarity of my spirit,
refined qi enters and the coarse impurities are removed.
I follow the gentle breeze to wander,
and arrive at Náncháo (南巢) to take a single breath.
I see the prince and stay with him,
examining the harmonious virtue of the One Qi.
He says:
"The Dao can be received,
but cannot be transmitted.
In its smallness, it has no interior,
in its greatness, it has no boundary.
Do not agitate your soul,
and it will be natural.
The One Qi is exceedingly spiritual,
existing in the middle of the night.
Await it with emptiness,
Before non-action;
myriad things are thereby completed,
this is the gate of virtue.
Having heard of the ultimate nobility, I then depart;
fleetingly, I shall go.
Following feather-men to Dānqiū,
remaining in the ancient land of immortality.
In the morning, I wash my hair in Tānggǔ,
in the evening, I dry my body on the Nine Yangs.
I sip the subtle essence of flying springs,
and cherish the brilliant blossoms of beautiful jade.
My jade-like complexion is radiant and my face is smooth,
my essence is pure and I begin to grow strong.
My form dissolves, becoming refined and graceful,
my spirit is profound and unrestrained.
I admire the flourishing virtue of the southern lands,
and the beautiful cassia trees that blossom in winter.
The mountains are desolate and devoid of beasts,
the fields are silent and without people.
I carry my soul and ascend on the clouds,
veiling the floating clouds as I embark on my journey.
I command the gatekeeper of Heaven to open the gate,
and push open the Chānghé gate to await me.
I summon Fēnglóng to lead the way,
and inquire about the dwelling place of Dàwēi.
I gather at Chóngyáng and enter the imperial palace,
arriving at the beginning of the cycle to view the pure capital.
In the morning, I set forth from Tài Yí;
in the evening, I first arrived at Wēi Lǘ.
I gathered my ten thousand chariots;
they surged and galloped alongside me.
I drove eight dragons, gracefully winding;
carrying cloud banners, long and flowing.
I erected the majestic rainbow's feathered staff;
the five colors mingled and dazzled.
My carriage was stately, rising and dipping;
the horses in my team were restless, prancing proudly.
The riders were entangled, mixed and disordered;
spreading in a colorful, boundless expanse, as we moved forward.
I grasped the reins and corrected the whip;
I was about to pass Jù Máng.
Passing Tài Hào, I turned to the right;
with Fēi Lián leading the way.
The sun was bright, but not yet fully shining;
I traversed heaven and earth directly.
The Earl of Wind acted as my vanguard;
the dust dissipated, leaving a cool breeze.
The phoenixes fanned their wings, bearing the banners;
I encountered Rù Shōu in the Western Wilderness.
I seized a comet as my pennon;
and raised the handle of the Big Dipper as my command flag.
The stars scattered in a confused manner, above and below;
I wandered through the flowing waves of startling mist.
The seasons were dim and vast;
I summoned Xuánwǔ and he came to join me.
Wénchāng was appointed to control the movements,
Selecting and appointing all the gods to proceed alongside.
The road is long and far,
Slowly moderating my pace and rising high.
The Yǔshī was sent to attend me on the left,
Léigōng served as my guard on the right.
Desiring to transcend the world and forget my homeland,
My thoughts are unrestrained, building lofty bridges.
Inwardly, I am joyful and pleased with myself,
Briefly indulging in pleasure for my own enjoyment.
Traversing the blue clouds, I roam and drift aimlessly,
Suddenly glancing down at my old home.
My driver is filled with sorrow,
The bordering horses look back but do not move forward.
Thinking of the past, I imagine it,
I sigh deeply and wipe away my tears.
Leisurely and slowly, I soar far away,
Briefly suppressing my desires and controlling myself.
Pointing to the Yánshén, I race straight ahead,
I shall go towards the southern doubts.
Viewing the vastness and formlessness beyond the boundaries,
I drift freely with the vast Wǎngxiàng.
Zhùróng was instructed to turn back the yoke,
Swiftly announcing to the Luán birds to welcome Mìfēi.
《Xiánchí》 was played and 《Chéngyún》 was performed,
The two goddesses performed 《Jiǔsháo》 with song.
I made Xiāng Líng play the zither,
And ordered Hǎi Ruò and Féng Yí to dance.
Dark dragons and other creatures emerged together,
Their forms twisting and coiling sinuously.
The female rainbow arched gracefully and added to the spectacle,
While phoenixes soared aloft and circled in flight.
The music was vast and without end,
Whereupon I lingered and hesitated.
Relaxing and controlling my joints, I galloped forth,
Surpassing the bounds of the cold gate.
I outstripped the swift wind at its source,
Following Zhuān Xū to the layered ice.
I traversed Xuán Míng by a winding path,
Seizing the opportune moment to glance back.
I summoned Qián Yíng to appear before me,
To lead me along the level road.
I surveyed the four wildernesses,
Circulating through the six deserts.
Ascending to the ranks of the stars,
Descending to gaze upon the great ravines.
Below, it was rugged with no ground,
Above, it was vast with no sky.
Looking fleetingly, there was nothing to see,
Listening confusedly, there was nothing to hear.
I transcended inaction to reach utmost purity,
And became a neighbor to the Great Beginning.
Divining a Dwelling Place.
Qū Yuán 屈原, having been exiled, for three years was unable to see the king again.
He exhausted his wisdom and devoted his loyalty,
but was obscured and blocked by slander.
His heart was troubled and his thoughts were disordered,
not knowing what path to follow.
He went to see the Grand Diviner Zhèng Zhān Yǐn 鄭詹尹, saying:
"I have some doubts
and wish to have you, sir, resolve them."
Zhān Yǐn 詹尹 then straightened his counting sticks and brushed the tortoise shell,
saying, "What instruction will you give me?"
Qū Yuán 屈原 said:
"Should I rather be sincerely and earnestly
simple and loyal?
Or should I be obsequious to those coming and going, so that there is no end to it?
Should I rather clear away the weeds
and till the soil diligently?
Or should I associate with great men
to achieve fame?
Should I rather speak frankly and without reservation
at the risk of endangering myself?
Or should I follow the customs of the world and seek wealth and honor
to prolong my life by evading danger?
Should I rather transcend the world and soar high
to preserve my true nature?
Or should I cringe and tremble,
and babble like a child
to serve women?
Should I rather be honest and upright
Would you purify yourself?
Or would you be artful and humorous,
as pliable as grease or soft leather,
in order to cleanse the pillars?
Would you rather hold your head high like a colt destined to travel a thousand *lǐ*?
Or would you drift like a duck on the water,
rising and falling with the waves,
stealing a way to preserve your body?
Would you rather resist the yoke with a *qíjì* (fine steed)?
Or would you follow the tracks of a slow horse?
Would you rather fly wing-to-wing with a *huánghú* (swan)?
Or would you compete with chickens and ducks for food?
Which of these is auspicious, which is inauspicious?
What should I leave, what should I follow?"
"The world is turbid and unclear,
a cicada's wing is considered heavy,
and a thousand *jūn* are considered light;
the *huángzhōng* (yellow bell) is destroyed and discarded,
and clay pots thunder;
slanderers are highly esteemed,
and worthy men are without name.
Alas, silent and still,
who knows my integrity!"
Zhān Yǐn then put down his divining sticks and apologized, saying:
"A *chǐ* (foot) has its limitations,
a *cùn* (inch) has its strengths,
things have their insufficiencies,
wisdom has its obscurities,
Calculation has its limits,
and the spirit has its inabilities.
To employ your ruler's heart,
and to execute your ruler's will,
divination by tortoise shells and milfoil stalks truly cannot understand affairs."
