Qū Yuán, having been exiled, wandered along the rivers and pools,
chanting while walking by the marshes.
His complexion was haggard,
and his appearance withered.
The fisherman saw him and asked,
"Are you not the Sānlǘ Dàfū?
Why have you come to this place?"
Qū Yuán said,
"The whole world is muddy, yet I alone am clear;
everyone is drunk, yet I alone am sober;
therefore, I have been exiled."
The fisherman said,
"A sage does not become fixated on things,
but is able to adapt to the times.
If the world is muddy,
why not stir its mud and churn its waves?
If everyone is drunk,
why not eat their dregs and drink their lees?
Why must you ponder deeply and hold yourself aloof,
thus bringing about your own exile?"
Qū Yuán said,
"I have heard that,
one who has newly washed his hair must flick the dust from his hat,
and one who has newly bathed must shake out his clothes.
How can I, with a body so pure,
accept defilement from worldly things?
I would rather go to the Xiāng River
and be buried in the bellies of the river fish.
How can I, with such gleaming whiteness,
allow myself to be covered in the dust of the world?"
The fisherman smiled broadly,
beat his oar, and left.
He sang:
"When the waters of the Cānglàng are clear,
I can wash my hat strings;
when the waters of the Cānglàng are muddy,
I can wash my feet."
Then he left, and did not speak with him again.
Nine Declarations
Alas, how sorrowful is the breath of autumn!
With a soughing sound,
the grasses and trees wither and decay,
with a desolate sound,
as if on a long journey,
climbing mountains and overlooking water,
seeing off someone about to return home.
How vast,
The sky is high and the air is clear;
solitary and still,
the floodwaters recede and the water is clear.
Sadly and mournfully, with increased sighs,
a slight chill penetrates the people.
Disappointed and desolate, restless and forlorn,
leaving the old and embracing the new.
Destitute and distressed,
an impoverished scholar loses his position and his ambition remains unfulfilled.
Empty and desolate,
a traveler is without friends.
Disappointed,
I privately pity myself.
The swallows flutter, bidding farewell to return home;
the cicadas are silent and still.
The geese fly south in a flock,
the *kūnjī* (a type of pheasant) chirps sadly.
Alone, I remain awake until dawn,
lamenting the crickets' nightly journey.
Time passes steadily past midday,
I am hampered, lingering without accomplishment!
Sadness, worry, poverty, and grief – alone I dwell in the emptiness.
There is a beautiful person whose heart I cannot fathom.
Leaving my hometown and family, I have come as a distant guest.
Surpassing carefree wandering, where do I now alight?
Concentrating on my lord, I cannot change;
my lord does not know this – what can I do?
Holding resentment, accumulating thoughts,
My heart is troubled and unsettled, I forget to eat.
I wish to see you once and tell you my thoughts,
But your heart, my lord, is different from mine.
The carriage is already harnessed, I will depart and return,
Unable to see you, my heart is wounded and grieved.
Leaning on the connected carriage rails, I heave a long sigh,
Tears streaming down, wetting the carriage bar.
Indignant and despairing, I cannot obtain [my desire],
My mind is confused and bewildered.
I privately pity myself to the utmost,
My heart pounds, truly upright.
August Heaven evenly divides the four seasons,
Yet I alone grieve for this desolate autumn.
The white dew has already fallen on all the grasses,
Suddenly scattering this *wútóng* and *qiū* tree.
Departing from the brightness of the white sun,
I am enveloped in the endlessness of the long night.
Leaving the luxuriant fragrance that was flourishing,
I wither and am sorrowful.
Autumn has already given early warning with the white dew,
Winter further emphasizes it with severe frost.
Gathering the vastness of early summer,
I am listless and hidden away.
The leaves are withered and colorless,
The branches are tangled and crisscrossed;
The radiant appearance is fading and will cease,
The boughs are faint and yellowish;
Alas for the withering of the xiāo xiāo shēn!
My form is consumed and bruised.
It is because they are mingled and about to fall,
I lament that they have missed their season and are out of place.
I grasp the reins and descend the steps,
I idly stroll to and fro.
The year rushes by and comes to an end,
I fear that my life will not last.
I grieve that I was born at an unfortunate time,
And encounter this tumultuous world.
Calmly and leisurely, I lean alone,
The crickets chirp in this western hall.
My heart trembles and shakes,
Why are there so many anxieties!
I look up at the bright moon and sigh,
I walk among the arrayed stars and seek the utmost clarity.
I secretly grieve that the huì flowers once bloomed,
Luxuriantly spreading throughout the rooms.
Why do the once blooming flowers bear no fruit,
But scatter and fly away with the wind and rain?
I thought you alone favored this huì,
But you are no different from the other fragrant plants.
Lamenting that my extraordinary thoughts cannot be communicated,
I will leave you and soar high.
My heart aches with sorrow and sadness,
I wish for one audience to clarify things.
Again, there is no resentment, yet we are separated,
My heart is tied in knots, increasing my sorrow.
How can I not be filled with melancholy, thinking of my lord?
The gates to my lord are ninefold.
Fierce dogs bark fiercely to greet me,
The passes are closed and impassable.
August Heaven overflows with autumn rain,
When will Mother Earth ever be dry?
I remain alone, guarding this barren place,
Looking up at the floating clouds and sighing eternally.
How skillful the world's customs are now,
Turning their backs on the plumb line and making changes in error!
They reject the *qí jì* (fine steed) and do not ride it,
But whip the inferior *nú tái* (nag) and take to the road.
Is it that the world lacks *qí jì* (fine steeds)?
It is truly that no one can skillfully control them.
Seeing that the one holding the reins is not the right person,
The *qú* (stallion) therefore leaps and goes far away.
Ducks and geese all feed on the *liáng zǎo* (fine grain and algae),
The *fèng* (phoenix) soars ever higher and aloft.
A round mortise and a square tenon,
I know for certain that they will clash and be difficult to join.
All the birds have places to perch,
The *fèng* (phoenix) alone is distraught and has nowhere to gather.
I wish to hold a gag in my mouth and remain silent,
Having once received my lord's generous kindness.
*Tài Gōng* (Grand Duke) was ninety years old before he became illustrious,
Truly he had not yet met his match.
Where does one say the *qíjì* go to?
Where does one say the *fènghuáng* roost?
Changing antiquity and altering customs, the world declines.
Today's horse assessors only value fatness.
The *qíjì* lies hidden and unseen,
The *fènghuáng* flies high and does not descend.
Even birds and beasts know to cherish virtue;
How can one say that worthy scholars do not reside here?
The *jì* does not quickly advance and seek service,
The *fèng* likewise does not greedily desire bait and rashly eat.
The ruler discards those far away and does not observe them;
Even if one wishes to be loyal, how can one achieve it?
Wishing to be silent and sever all ties,
I secretly dare not forget the initial great kindness.
I am alone, grieving that it wounds people;
Relying on melancholy, what is the limit?
Frost and dew descend miserably and mingled together,
In my heart, I still hoped it would not come to pass.
Sleet and snow swirl and increase,
Then I knew that the arrival of fate was near.
Wishing to seek luck and have something to wait for,
To drift aimlessly and die alongside the wild grass.
Wishing to go of my own accord and travel directly,
The road is blocked and impassable.
Wishing to follow the path and drive smoothly,
Yet I do not know where to follow.
Being lost in the middle of the road,
I oppress myself and study recitation.
My nature is foolish, simple, and narrow-minded,
truly not yet having attained composure.
I admire Shēn Bāoxū's 申包胥 vigorous spirit,
yet fear the times are not stable.
How skilled and clever are the customs of the time!
They abolish the compass and square and alter the grooves.
I alone am upright and do not follow them,
wishing to emulate the teachings left behind by the former sages.
To be prominent and honored in a corrupt world
is not what my heart desires.
Rather than being famous without righteousness,
I would rather be impoverished and uphold high principles.
I do not steal food to be full,
nor do I carelessly seek clothes to be warm.
I secretly admire the customs left behind by the poets,
and wish to entrust my will to plain living.
My progress is hindered and abrupt, without beginning or end,
adrift, vast and boundless.
Without clothes or fur to ward off the winter,
I fear I will suddenly die and not see the spring.
Observing the beautiful tips of autumn's long night,
my heart is troubled and sorrowful.
Spring and autumn pass swiftly as the days grow long,
yet I am full of melancholy and self-pity.
The four seasons alternate and the year ends,
yin and yang cannot be paired together.
The bright sun wanes and is about to set,
The bright moon wanes and diminishes.
The years rush by and come to an end,
Old age slowly and increasingly slackens.
My heart is delighted and hopes for each day,
Yet I am forlorn and without hope.
In my heart, there is a deep, sorrowful grief,
I sigh deeply and increase my sobs.
The years flow on day by day,
Old age is vast and without a place to rest.
I strive diligently and hope for advancement,
But I am hindered, delayed, and hesitate.
Why do the floating clouds spread so widely,
Violently obscuring this bright moon!
My loyalty is clear and I wish to be seen,
But it is dim and obscured, and cannot reach [the ruler].
I wish the bright sun would shine forth,
But the clouds are heavy and obscure it.
I secretly cannot comfort myself and desire to be loyal,
But perhaps I am stained and defiled.
Yáo and Shùn walked with upright conduct,
Understanding the darkness and reaching for the heavens.
Why is there such treacherous jealousy,
To be falsely accused of unkindness?
The bright illumination of the sun and moon,
Still has darkness and flaws.
How much more so the affairs of a state,
Also, there are many reasons for them to be closely attached.
Covered by the lotus canopy, so peaceful and leisurely,
yet vast and unrestrainable.
Already arrogant and boasting of military prowess,
relying on the uprightness of those on the left and right.
Hating and resenting the beautiful conduct of Lún (惀),
favoring the generosity of the ladies.
The multitude stumbles forward day by day,
while beauty surpasses and goes beyond.
The farmers cease plowing and linger leisurely,
fearing the fields will become overgrown with weeds.
Affairs are continuous and full of personal interests,
secretly lamenting the future dangers and failures.
The world is uniform and dazzling,
how can praise and blame be so obscure!
Now adorning oneself and peering into the mirror,
later one might still be able to hide away.
I wish to entrust words to the shooting star,
but it is so swift and hard to grasp.
Finally, these floating clouds block everything,
causing darkness and lack of light below.
Yáo (堯) and Shùn (舜) both had those they promoted and entrusted,
therefore they could rest their heads high and be content.
Since there was no resentment toward the world,
why would their hearts feel apprehension?
Riding on the freely galloping Qíjì (騏驥) horse,
why would one need forceful whipping?
I realize that walls and moats are not dependable;
though heavily armored, what use is it?
Wheeling about restlessly without end;
confused and muddled, my sorrow constricts.
Living in this world is like merely passing through;
without accomplishing anything, there is no effect.
I wish to sink into obscurity and not be seen;
yet still I desire to spread my name throughout the world.
But wandering broadly and not meeting with success;
I am simply foolishly vexing myself with bitterness.
Vast and boundless, without limit;
suddenly soaring, where shall I alight?
If the state has a Jì 驥 steed and does not know how to ride it;
why do they rush about frantically searching for another?
Níng Qī 甯戚 sang beneath the chariot;
Duke Huán 桓公 heard him and recognized his worth.
Without Bó Lè 伯樂 to assess talent well;
who now can be sent to praise me?
I do not weep to merely ease my worries;
but only by focusing my mind can I achieve it.
My pure and sincere desire is to be loyal;
but jealousy causes me to be separated and blocked.
I wish to be granted this unworthy body and to part ways;
to release my will to wander in the clouds.
Riding on the congealed essence of breath;
galloping among the deep stillness of the gods.
With white rainbows as my team, soft and flowing;
Passing through the abundant spirits.
On the left, the luxuriant Zhū Què (Vermilion Bird),
on the right, the leaping Cāng Lóng (Azure Dragon).
Attached are the rumbling Léi Shī (Masters of Thunder),
communicating with the hurrying Fēi Lián (God of the Wind).
In the front, the jingling light carriages,
in the rear, the following baggage carts.
Carrying cloud banners that undulate,
escorted by mounted guards in orderly array.
Calculating the unchangeable constancy,
I wish to pursue it and make it good.
Relying on the great virtue of majestic Heaven,
it returns, and you, my lord, are unharmed.

my body adhering to righteousness, never tarnished.
Possessing this great virtue,
I was drawn by custom into wild and impure ways.
Having no way to examine this great virtue above,
I long suffered misfortune and sorrow.

Soul, return!

obtain human flesh for sacrifice,
and use their bones to make minced meat sauce.

devouring people to nourish their hearts.
Return!

Soul, return! The harm of the west,
is shifting sands for a thousand *lǐ*.

being ground to dust and unstoppable.

Soul, return!

Return!

Soul, return!

Return!

Moth eyebrows and beautiful eyes, eyes emitting light.

Separate pavilion and long curtains, waiting on the lord in leisure.
Jade curtains and emerald canopies, adorn the high hall.
Red walls and sanded panels, black jade beams.

Sitting in the hall, leaning on the railing, overlooking the winding pond.
Lotuses just beginning to bloom, mingled with water caltrops and lotus.
Purple stalk screens, with patterned borders like waves.

Carriages are low, infantry and cavalry arrayed.

Soul and spirit, return! Do not wander far away.
